title: Replication Fork Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll man the replication fork — helicase, polymerase, leading and lagging strands.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology DNA Replication — replication fork, helicase, DNA polymerase III, primers, Okazaki fragments and ligase.
final_note: You learned how helicase unwinds DNA, primase lays RNA primers, DNA polymerase III extends 5' to 3' continuously on the leading strand and discontinuously on the lagging, and ligase seals fragments.

concepts.def: Y-shaped region where DNA is being unwound and copied
Breaks H-bonds between bases, unwinds the double helix
Lays down short RNA primers — needed for DNA polymerase to start
Main replicating enzyme — adds nucleotides 5' to 3'
Synthesised in Okazaki fragments away from the fork

walkthroughs.body_html:
Replication begins at an origin of replication.

1. Helicase binds and unwinds the double helix → two replication forks moving in opposite directions.
2. Single-strand binding proteins keep strands apart.
3. Topoisomerase relieves the supercoiling ahead of the fork by cutting and resealing.

DNA polymerase can't start a strand from scratch — it can only extend an existing 3' OH.

Primase lays down a short RNA primer with a free 3' end.

DNA polymerase III then adds DNA nucleotides 5' to 3', complementary to the template (A-T, C-G), forming phosphodiester bonds in the backbone.

The two template strands run antiparallel — only one can be copied continuously towards the fork.

Leading strand — one primer, continuous synthesis.

Lagging strand — many primers, short pieces called Okazaki fragments made away from the fork.

DNA polymerase I replaces the RNA primers with DNA, then DNA ligase joins the fragments by forming the final phosphodiester bonds.

Result: two identical daughter molecules.

mcqs.q: Which enzyme unwinds the DNA double helix at the replication fork?
Why is the lagging strand made in fragments?
options: DNA polymerase only synthesises 5' to 3', and the strand runs away from the fork

numericals.q: If the leading strand needs 1 primer, and the lagging strand needs 8 primers, how many primers are needed in total for this fork?

free_texts.q: What is the name of the short RNA molecules laid down by primase to start DNA synthesis? One word.
